GL Labs from the horror game "Spooky's Jumpscare Mansion" (formerly "Spooky's House of Jumpscares" due to a legal dispute) is a pretty clear reference to the SCP foundation. item.title: First SCP
item.description: Why has no one yet thought of an SCP with this property?
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP

Genre (Optional):

Page Layout (Optional):

Elevator Pitch: The SCP is an extradimensional space that traps people inside if they know that the SCP exists. It was made as a containment vessel for something really dangerous.

Central Narrative: The SCP was created by an anomalous person to deal with a dangerous anomaly of yet unknown nature. Its properties ensure that knowledge of the SCP will never exist outside of it, therefore ensuring that the entity contained within will never be known to the outside world. The Foundation decides to investigate a series of disappearances which leads them to discover the SCP. When the MTF get inside they learn of the scip's effects from the person which results in them unable to leave the SCP. They compile a document describing the SCP before taking amnestics. The Amnestics removed their knowledge of the SCP, allowing them to return to site. When the SCP documentation is read, the reader will be immediately teleported to the SCP, requiring them to consume amnestics to leave.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: I've not yet seen an SCP with effects which are caused by someone knowing them. It's just a very goood concept to think about. In fact, I don't know why I haven't read an SCP with this property, because it is just so obvious.

Additional Notes: The dangerous entity could be another SCP. This is just about the location that it is contained within and its property.
Also, I don't know how is the article going to work in-universe because everyone who reads the article and therefore becomes aware of the existence of the SCP will be pulled into it.

item.title: Requesting greenlight for SCP (Tune in Next Time)
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Mainly historical, a bit of horror, I suppose

Page Layout (Optional): Basic layout; containment procedures, test logs, possibly a picture

Elevator Pitch: SCP-XXXX is a radio tower built somewhere around the 1980s located around Ballard, Utah, and has not been fed power since its abandonment somewhere between 1985 and 1990. The tower broadcasts a radio signal which is still able to be picked up by radios approximately six miles in the surrounding area. The signal is static at most times save for an AI voice announcing a web address every five hours. The address seems to be the contact information for the radio tower operators. But there have been four (4) recorded instances of there being an actual being speaking through the signal.

Central Narrative: When the static clears on the signal a being deemed SCP-XXXX-A speaks through the signal in a deep, muffled voice. In all cases of this occurring, the being has announced the first and last name of a person, followed by a word and a series of four seemingly random numbers after which the signal returns to static.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Within the time ranging from two hours to three weeks, the person which the name belongs is attacked by an anomalous creature. The hostility and overall danger of the creature vary with each encounter with some merely beating or bruising the victim, to consuming them. The time in which SCP-XXXX-A has existed is currently unknown with the first record of the being dating back to the early sixteen hundreds with an Englishman describing "a cloaked figure who sat at tavern tables requesting bizarre items in exchange for the punishment of another". SCP-XXXX-A is capable of being contacted currently through an email which is posted on SCP-XXXX's website. Three of the four people responsible for the recorded attacks have been subdued and administered class-B amnestics. The whereabouts of the last person are currently unknown.

Additional Notes: No additional notes.

item.title: The Oreads
item.description: After a Battle So Great, all that remains is Dust.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): History, Fantasy

Page Layout (Optional): ACS

+ Idea here
- Long, I know

Elevator Pitch: SCP is a small, 50m long beach located near Kandestederne, Denmark. In the event an individual makes contact with the sand, it will respond to the conscious thoughts of that individual and shift into a variety of structures accordingly. With concentration, The sand can also emulate the structures physical (not chemical) properties, such as weight, ductility, pigment and conductivity. However, it can't take the form of non-solids. The sand only acts this way if it's on the beach. If the sand is taken 5 meters away from the beach, the sand will start vibrating and pulsating before suddenly becoming inactive. The sand also appears to have some degree of sapience/conscious and can react if communicated with or attacked.

Central Narrative: When the Foundation first discovered the beach (in the 1950s), it was acting aggressive and attacked anyone who attempted to walk upon it. Through research and discussions with the locals, the Foundation discover one of them is in possession of a jar of sand which they took from the beach after discovering it's strange properties. The sand was then returned and the beach instantly began cooperating.

After some experiments with the sand, researchers managed to discover it could understand Koine Greek. After finding a translater, the Foundation were able to discover that the sand is in fact the remnants of the Oread, the mountain nymphs from Greek Mythology. The Oreads reveal that long ago, they lost their true form in a battle with a monstrous sea creature1, resulting in them taking on their current sand from. In their sand form, they're conscious was spread so thin, only they're instinct to join back together remained. This was difficult as their parts were spread across the world via ocean currents. The beach is a collection of their remnants who've managed to form a collective conscious. However, it's weak enough to be influenced by a stronger mind, resulting in the structures it creates.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: This article is kind of sad. We're meant to feel sorry for the Oreads. They desperately want to return to their old forms but The Foundation is unable to help as 1. it would take forever for every sand particle to randomly end up on the beach and 2. how can The Foundation possibly give them back their true form if they don't know who's who and what they look like.

item.title: [Seeking Greenlight] A sentient entity formed from a psychic virus
item.description: An otherwise benign virus, present in nearly every human, creates a sentient entity which experiences the sensations of every infected person.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Drama/ (maybe) Comedy

Page Layout: Since this would be my first SCP, it will remain simple, with standard containment/description and a couple addendums.

Elevator Pitch: Nearly every human hosts a benign virus, located in their brain, which emits psychic signals to virus cells in other hosts. These cells combine, like neurons in a brain, to form a sentient entity. This entity experiences the sensory inputs of every infected individual, motivating it to act in the interest of maximizing human pleasure and minimizing human pain. The entity is able to "possess" the bodies of a small number of infected humans at a time, and uses this ability to communicate.

Central Narrative: Containment procedures will first outline Foundation contingency plans for vaccinating all staff and the general population, before detailing the process of the Foundation conducting yearly negotiations with the the entity for its cooperation. The result of these negotiations is an agreement wherein the entity assists the foundation through its abilities, while the Foundation takes limited actions to influence national and international politics in ways the entity believes will increase collective happiness. The entity has over the years made increasingly extreme demands, and the Foundation privately fears they create a high risk of exposure. Addendums include conversations with the entity, as well as the text of the agreement between it and the Foundation

Hook/Attention-Grabber: As a result of experiencing vast sensory input from large numbers of people, the entity has a unique personality and manner of speaking, constantly switching languages and often communicating in references to popular culture (i.e. quotes from widely-viewed movies, news and sports broadcasts, and printed media). The entity also has a skewed view of humanity, discounting freedom of action in favor of collective interests.

Additional Notes:

1. Considering adding a comedic edge to the story by having the entity be obsessed with a revival of its favorite television show, "The Andy Griffith Show," demanding that the Foundation resurrect the show's dead cast members so that new episodes can be viewed by the infected public.

2. I don't think this concept is particularly original, and don't have exhaustive knowledge of the SCP database, so please tell me if this has already been done in some form.

3. I have already written the first draft of an article, so if sharing that would be helpful to deciding whether or not to greenlight, please let me know.

item.title: The Emotional Support Pet - Seeking Greenlights
item.description: A benefical Keter anomaly- has anyone done an idea like this already?
item.content:encoded:
The Emotional Support Pet

Seeking Greenlights: Yes.

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: What is the basic core idea? Use a bullet point list if necessary.

An adorable kitten, puppy or bunny who appears to meet people suffering from trauma, depression, or various other emotional and mental health issues, and who gets them to pet it, which causes the individual in question to heal from the issue until they no longer have need of such healing. In certain cases, such as in the case of abuse or situations serving to only exasperate the issues which the individual needs help with, the animal companion will align a series of events to extract the individual from the situation before the ensuing treatment.

Actually feeds off of both mental and emotional trauma as well as the excess positive energy which is produced during the healing process and for a short while afterwards. Doesn’t need to cause what it feeds off of and change from symbiosis to parasitism due to the huge number of people already suffering from these problems.

Class: Keter

Central Narrative: Helps to explain why humanity isn’t universally traumatized other than the low number of anomalous in the world, because there’s a huge amount and this world needs some form of anomalous therapist, of which there are far too few already.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Unsure, really only looking to post this idea if there isn’t already a similar enough instance to this prospective SCP. Mostly a hurt/comfort idea, but it can easily veer into horror if the anomalous object sees that the only way to fully heal the individual includes such events.

Additional Notes: Due to its teleportation to its ‘patients’ and how it literally bends probability to its own ends, which just so happy to most often be beneficial to humanity, as well as the unknown number of instances of this ‘species’ in this world, how do you think this would even be contained? Would it? And, again, has someone already written something like this?

So, this is my first potential contribution, so what do you guys think?

item.title: SCP idea, seeking greenlight: The Grand Conspiracy
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: An infohazard that causes no side effects whatsoever unless someone tries to look into the nature of its existence. Anyone who attempts such will become more and more unstable as they begin to obsess over researching the SCP, coming up with theories concerning it that become increasingly irrational as their mental state decreases, eventually driving them to insanity. Essentially, the SCP makes anyone who tries to figure out what it is into a deranged conspiracy theorist.

Central Narrative: The perspective of an unfortunate researcher, showcasing his descent into insanity.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: This SCP isn’t one of those "kills you as soon as you realize it exists" things - it works by lowering your intellect/mental stability until you're not able to even come close to understanding it. For example, an experienced scientist might start off with a somewhat accurate hypothesis, only to wind up believing that it was created by Hitler's secret grandchild in Area 51 a week later. And considering that it has no outward anomalous effects, it could potentially have already infected every person on the planet undetected - alternatively, it could be some kind of virus with a malicious purpose that the Foundation will never be able to come close to discovering.

Additional Notes: I haven't yet figured out some parts of this, like how exactly the Foundation would discover this SCP exists - I can work out the finer details when I start drafting. For now, I just want to know if this would be something people are interested in reading.

item.title: Seeking Greenlight: SCP idea

Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): vehicle / extradimensional / ad-astra

Elevator Pitch: A dead space ship from the future, which has an invisible entity on board that kills everyone once it is in atmospheric environment.

Central Narrative: The SCP is divided into 2 parts, the ship and the entity. The ship is an advanced human design (not Foundation) that at the current time should not exist. The crew has been murdered by the entity and the ship has been vented. One of the Foundation researchers notes a couple of things about the ship (none of which are anomalous, making it unknow how it got to our time).

The entity can be heard walking around the ship and is pretty harmless in void. It can jump between ships and when in any atmosphere, arms come from the walls, pulling people inside the walls and killing them in the process. The entity was not originally on the ship, its origin is unknown.

The team sent to explore the ship finds disfigured humans basically melted into the ships structure. After a while the team is killed by the entity except for 2 members who still die after a while because they run out of oxygen and there is no help coming.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The entity on board the ship is only dangerous under atmospheric pressure but humans need that to survive.

Additional Notes: Hope it's not too generic horror.

item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: No

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Drama, Mystery.

Elevator Pitch: Robotic entity, like a living humanoid machine, found in the middle of the forest in Sweden. The entity is in a dormant state until 2 members of the cult "The children of the Scarlet King" perform a ritual to awaken it.

Central Narrative: The SCP seems to be confused when it arrives at the Foundation. It doesn't know (or remember) what a human is. It has the ability to bend reality but does it rarely. The entity is somewhat dangerous but poses no real threat to the Foundation. However its memories slowly start to come back in small chunks… piecing together what it really is and why it is here.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: It tries to assassinate SCP-999. What was the name of that cult again? The children of the Scarlet King? Perhaps there's something bigger here… something that will be added in containment breach logs and interviews later in the future.

Additional Notes: Assassinate is a strong word. It more just attacks SCP-999 having no idea why it does this. Of course the attempt fails and the entity just gets itself hurt.

The scp is also known as "A Face full of Stars because the SCP greatly resembles that of a robotic entity from a reboot of a old tv show about traveling space. The netflix lost in space reboot.

One of the addendums, explaining how the scp was discovered, also slightly explains how the netflix reboot is actually made by one of the cultists who was given amnestic treatment and a fake name, but couldnt forget what the scp looked like.

item.title: Looking for Greenlights | The Stardust Solution
item.description: A microscopic baby universe prepared to unleash its explosive potential.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: This SCP, nicknamed "The Stardust Solution", is a microscopic singularity that is the first stage of a universe. It absorbs energy and matter at a subatomic level, increasing its density. At some point in time it will fail to contain its own density and explode instead of collapsing, creating a second Big Bang.

A stone tablet found near it indicates that some form of SCP created the singularity with the purpose of restarting the universe—for the second time.

Central Narrative: The article focuses on the perspective of two researchers assigned to this SCP—Doctors Stonewood and Jordan. The volatile nature of the SCP warrants the creation of a small Foundation outpost, as storing other SCPs near the singularity is hazardous.

After describing the discovery of the SCP, the file turns to a series of interviews.

Interview One presents Stonewood and Jordan as colleagues speaking about the threat the singularity presents. As Jordan explains the nature of the SCP to Stonewood, he articulates that he has given up hope. The singularity will continue absorbing energy until it ruptures, and they know nothing about how to stop it. Jordan also believes that it doesn't deserve to be an SCP—the phenomena is a natural state of the universe (they have not yet translated the stone tablet).

Stonewood is far more optimistic, and he convinces Jordan to help him develop a way to slow down the singularity, limiting the likelihood that it will rupture anytime soon. The interview ends on a hopeful note—despite not knowing how to stop the anomaly from eventually rupturing and causing an XK scenario, they pledge themselves to seeking the answers.

Interview Two is set six months later. The stone tablet has been restored and is now readable, and Stonewood is interviewing the linguist who translated it. The linguist gives Stonewood the translation written in English. Upon reading it, he grows agitated and leaves the interview, seeking Doctor Jordan.

The addendum reveals the translation: a command from a being ordering his "son" to erase the "narrative" that he sees as a failure. The writing ends with a vow: "I promise I will not make the same mistakes the third time around."

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The Foundation has dealt with a ridiculous amount of anomalies, but it made me wonder: what if another SCP got sick of living in a world full of anomalies and decided to try to "correct" it?

item.title: Looking for Greenlights | The Hapless Helper
item.description: An SCP eager to help, but can end up causing unintended side effects.
item.content:encoded:
The Hapless Helper
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Emotional/Mystery

Elevator Pitch:
Based on the Thumbling (Grimm Fairytale)
- A tiny man the size of a thumb that seeks to help others.
- It can inadvertently hinder those it tries to help.
- SCP becomes pale and sickly if it cannot provide aid to others.

Central Narrative:

- SCP first appeared to keep a peasant family company.
- It travelled the world, aiming to help, typically causing harm, but being legitimately helpful on several occasions.

- An example of a hindrance was when the SCP aiming to ‘help’ robbers burgling a cottage. It loudly performed the actions it was told, waking the residents.
- The SCP left, assuming it helped the family when in actuality, it ended up causing the family to be shot after they tried confronting the robbers.

- Appeared and kept in contact with a girl it calls Allison who would later become a worker in the SCP Foundation, who joined in order to find the Thumbling once more.
- After intense review, the SCP was allowed to accompany scientists and help within the site it is located at.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Concise article with an interview log to explain the SCP’s connection to Alison.

Additional Notes: I want to keep the focus of the article on the mysteries surrounding the SCP and its desire to connect with members of the Foundation. I generally want the article to feel like the SCP is a positive influence but with a slight hint of dread that something may go wrong in the future.

(I edited the mention of Alison being an O5 member to her being a regular worker in the SCP Foundation)

item.title: An Infinitely Expanding Room That Feeds Off Of Your Subconscious.
item.content:encoded:
A potential GoI or collective group of SCPs.

Please note I am reposting this as I did not use the correct format for an SCP submission in my previous post. My apologies.

Seeking Greenlights: Yes.

Page Type: SCP Article/GoI Format

Genre (Optional): Action/Mystery

Elevator Pitch: A room SCP that has a few anomalous properties. First of all, it is effectively an infinite white void on the inside, which then feeds off of your thoughts and subconscious to create an inconceivable, strange reality inside. Second, the anomalous properties will not take place if you enter the room without knocking. Third, if you venture deep enough, you will find 13 other rooms. The premise here is that there are 13 other rooms with similar anomalous properties, that being, they're all detached rooms, they all won't activate unless you knock, and they all have the same feature where if you venture deep enough, you'll find somewhat of a link to the other 13 rooms. This is what confirmed the link between these SCPs, and what caused them to identify them collectively as, essentially, one.

Central Narrative: This SCP destroyed a suburb, named Billowgreens. Where's Billowgreens, you ask? The premise here is that everyone who knew about Billowgreens was given Class-A amnestics, to not remember the disaster. It was caused by an accident, where a person walked in and out of the room and unfortunately spread the "room reality" outside into the real world, which then tore apart "real reality" and became more and more chaotic the more people were stepping in it. It was eventually quarantined, and what was once Billowgreens is now a containment site for this new reality,

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Reality bending room SCP that spreads like a virus once it's outside the room. Destroyed an entire suburb.

Additional Notes: As previously mentioned, i believe this could work as a new GoI, or a collective group of these 14 room SCPs.

item.title: The Imitation Blob
item.description: My idea for my first SCP, one that humanizes the D-Class a little more by ironically, turning a D-Class into anything but a human.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlight: Yes
Page Type: SCP article
Genre: Horror/Drama
Elevator Pitch: A Blob capable of transforming into anything in consumes, and the disaster that occurs when it eats a D-Class.
Central Narritve:
The Imatation Blob's normal behavior is freindly and curious, until introduced to a living creature via touch.

Upon being exposed to a living creature, the blob will trap the hand or foot of its victim with it's super sticky body then being to swell in size until it encompasses them, dissolving them in seconds.

The Blob will then transform into a perfect replica of it's victim and adopt the victims mannerisms until it eats something else, at which point it will revert back to it's base form and resume normal behavior.

+ show block
– hide block

After multiple tests on The Blob, they test it with a D-class. The Blob behaves exactly the same throughout most of the test, until it dissolves the D-Class. Strangely, it remaines in it's blob form for 10 minutes, studying itself. Afterwards The Blob transformed into a unknown creature and breaches containment.

The Blob then proceededs to rampage through the site, taking the form of multiple creatures, many anomalous and previously unknown to the foundation. Before it's recontained. It kills multiple workers and absorbs both an instance of SCP-939 and an instance of SCP-3199.No D-Class are harmed during the breach, and The Blob strangely targets Security Gaurds and Reaserchers accompanied by D-Class above others.

Afterwards it behaves extremely differently, it is aggressive and makes multiple attempts to breach containment.

This is because, instead of The Blob temporily replicating the physical appearence and behavior of the D-Class, it instead copies it's mind without replicating it's physical appearance, gaining sentience and a grudge against he Foundation as well as a fondness and sense of comradery towards D-Class.

It's containment procedures now require it be contained in a cell capable of containing as many different SCPs as possible, for it is unknown how many creatures The Blob is capable of replicating now. In the event The Blob does breach containment, Security Gaurds are instructed to take D-class into a secured intercom room. Then the Security Gaurds are instructed to threaten to terminate D-Class if The Blob does not return to containment, followed byterminateing 1 D-Class every minute until The Blob returns to containment, or MTF squad arrives.

Attention Grabber: Basically, I find the potential for sympathetic or humanized D-Class severely underutilized and I wanted to show more of the comradery between the members of D-class.

item.title: Critter Profile: Emma and Cream!
item.content:encoded:

Page Type: GoI Format

Page Layout: A "password protected" link to click to reveal the page

Elevator Pitch: Emma the fire-spewing Texas horned lizard fares better when placed by Cream the goose who lays golden eggs — so much better, in fact, that she grows beyond her expected size. When a robber stops by to steal the goose, he gets more than he bargained for.

Central Narrative: Emma is a Texas horned lizard who shoots fire from her eyes instead of blood. She comes in clutching a gold ring, which is taken and sold, Wilson’s not realizing its importance. Emma then becomes smaller and more lethargic by the day, prompting concern from staff at Wilson's.

Cream is a goose who lays golden eggs which turn into normal eggs after a few hours. The page notes that there have been multiple inquiries and Cream is not up for adoption. When Cream gets transported past Emma’s terrarium for a checkup, Emma perks up and rushes to the front.

Wilson’s staff decide to put the two in enclosures next to each other and Emma starts healing with the proximity to gold. The two seem to like each other. Emma starts growing much larger than a horned lizard usually gets. Once she is large enough that her safety would no longer be a concern, Emma and Cream are placed together for short periods under close supervision. The two form a close bond, both showing signs of distress whenever they are separated.

In the email at the bottom, we learn of a Wilson’s overnight staff member hearing human screams along with distress calls from many of the animals. When they investigate, they find a robber who had tried to break into Cream's enclosure with a carrying cage. His hand is chewed off and he has severe burns all across his body. The lock to Emma's enclosure has melted open from the inside, but Emma is sitting inside near the wall that separates her from Cream. The robber is rushed to the hospital and the email suggests the web page be put under password protection in the future to avoid similar incidents — thus the password requirement at the beginning of the page.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Wilson's gets a sort-of dragon. Two animals make unlikely friends.

item.title: SCP - Kraken Mare
item.description: An anomalous ecosystem on Titan.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Science Fiction

Page Layout (Optional): Standard SCP article.

Elevator Pitch: There's an alien ecosystem in Kraken Mare, the largest of Titan's liquid methane seas. The anomaly is that the life there isn't really alien at all - all the organisms there are copies of marine life from Earth's Cretaceous seas, modified on the chemical level to survive Titan's conditions but unchanged on the macro scale. So rather than aliens swimming in methane, there are mosasaurs and ammonites instead.

Central Narrative: The central narrative is the mystery of how prehistoric animals ended up living on Titan. The Foundation first found the anomaly when a NASA probe to Kraken Mare got eaten - containment focuses on keeping information from getting out rather than doing anything on Titan itself. Eventually the Foundation sends another probe to explore Kraken Mare. The exploration log ends with a plinth on the seafloor that lists the surface liquids and basic biochemical reactions found on Earth, Titan, and an unknown third world with sulfuric acid seas. The implication is that aliens copy-pasted an ecosystem from one liquid medium to another, and did the same elsewhere, for reasons unknown.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: I think it's a fun mix between aliens and dinosaurs, combining real-life sea monsters with exotic hypothetical biochemistry. The story also ends with the revelation that powerful anomalous beings once came to Earth and, for once, did something pretty benign.

Additional Notes: I'm thinking about having the plinth be written in Ortothan, just to tie the SCP into something bigger and make it feel more connected to some other space SCPs.

item.title: Men Are Expendable
item.description: "We do not need men anymore"
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlight : Yes

Page Type : SCP Article

Genre : Emotional ?

Elevator Pitch : Based on an old African legend

- An SCP that allows a woman to become pregnant without having any sexual intercourse with a man

- Upon activation, the SCP “steals” something fundamentally valuable from the user. It can be anything : an object, a body part, memories, emotions… basically anything that belongs to the user.

- The children resulting from this pregnancy will always show great strength, intelligence and especially great charisma, but the males will be sterile.

Narrative :

+ show block
– hide block

The Foundation received reports of a secret tribe located somewhere in Africa, in which men and women were showing incredible physical and mental abilities. It’s inhabitants didn’t show any sign of hostility towards the agents that were sent to the place.

Upon investigating, the agents discovered that the tribe worshipped a wooden doll. Thanks to the efforts of the Foundation’s linguists, the present personnel was able to engage in a discussion with the aborigens, and discovered the abnormal effects of the said doll. Curiously, most of the tribesman claimed to have a woman as their parent, while the idea of a [male] father seemed strange to them. Every man and woman in the tribe were born as a result of the object’s effect.

The doll seems to activate its properties when being held by a fertile biological woman, between the age of 16 and 42. The said woman will show signs of pregnancy after a period of 2 months ; while the gestation time varies from 9 months to 1 year. The process cannot be activated if the woman who is holding the object despises children or doesn't want to have any. The way of how the wooden doll begats the pregnancy is unknown. However, upon the birth of her children, the woman will find herself robbed from something that is greatly valuable to her. This includes physical objects, body parts, abstract elements (such as beauty), and in some cases, emotions. The children born this way present incredible strength, intelligence and a great cognitive capacity. They do not present any anomaly, despite the males : they seem to be born without testicles and 'vas deferens' tubes, which causes sterility.

Hook/Attention-Grabber : I find this object quite interesting because it surrounds the idea of abandonment. I also present a tribal society in which men are not necessary anymore (which is quite scary for me, as a male).

Additional notes : Most of women of the tribe present weird characteristics, such as an absence of eyes, arms, hairs, or even the ability to speak, hear or see (despite having the necessary organs).

Elevator Pitch: The first anomaly is a child in a hazmat suit who's composed of 40% of the same materials found in a hydrogen bomb. The child was discovered in an abandoned town in Northern Russia after reports of unusual levels of radiation.

Due to being highly radioactive, the Foundation but him in a secure steel room. Even with its suit, contact with it results in severe radiation poisoning. The anomaly appears to have 3rd degree burns across its body, although it claims to suffer no physical pain from the burns.

The child also carries a backpack with 10 out of ordered issues of the Incredible Hulk.

It claims that it was left behind by their "older brother" in the town. It also talks about how its "Mother" used to care for them but she soon died forcing the two to depart for a new home.

The older brother is the second anomaly. It is an entity described to have "white noise" and " a dark figure". The entity only appeared once to take back the hazmat child due to the Foundation's "mistreatment" of them. The entity emits extremely high levels of radiation even in a 1-mile radius. It also affects electronic devices and signals rendering them dysfunctional. The entity also seems to have a psychic connection to the child, demonstrated when the child warns the Foundation that he is coming to pick him up.

Central Narrative: A foundation researcher will interview the child and will learn things about his older brother and Mother. But as the interviews go on, it becomes increasingly that the child keeping secrets. Central Narrative: the anomalous entity would first be discovered after the latest victim in a string of murder was brought to the attention of the foundation. Agents disguised as Federal agents would confiscate the recent body as well as all files on previous victims. After transferring the corpse to a foundation facility, one of the retrieval agents would discover an tattoo of unknown origin on his back after feeling a stinging sensation and seeing the scp taking the form of extinct species of Kaprosuchus. After the agents death from the scp, the skin of the agents back was removed, preserved and placed in a frame with the scp still in place with physical contact being heavily restricted to prevent containment breaches.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The ‘ink’ comprising of both the scp and the wounds it inflicts would contain partial dna mixed in with the normal content of the tattoo ink. Its main way of hunting would appear to try and make its prey paranoid all the while it toys with its prey.

Additional Notes: As stated, normal means one would take to remove a tattoo does not seem to work with the person attempting to remove the entity reporting feeling unnerved and/or receive tattooed markings in the form of self defensive slashes or bites

item.title: SCP-5133
item.content:encoded: Not a big fan of 'dangerous SCP just wandering around because we can't figure out Contain' and I don't think there's any good reason to not make it more-easily containable.
